+# Athena++ solar-wind crosscheck assessment
+
+Assessment only: no solar-wind problem generator or Athena core changes have
+been implemented. The existing independent Brio-Wu reference uses the pinned
+Princeton Athena++ dependency outside the project.
+
+A controlled 3D crosscheck is computationally tractable. The pinned source
+already supports spherical-polar coordinates, face-centered constrained
+transport, HLLD, PLM/characteristic reconstruction, fixed gamma, built-in
+point-mass gravity (`problem/GM`), user boundary callbacks, and binary VTK
+output without HDF5. Coordinates can directly use AU, day and the existing
+proton-density normalization. The fixed solar-equatorial coordinate frame,
+periodic longitude and latitude wedge can match the existing model.
+
+The main interfaces are `Mesh::InitUserMeshData`,
+`MeshBlock::ProblemGenerator`, `EnrollUserBoundaryFunction`, and optional
+`UserWorkInLoop`/history hooks. Native VTK can be postprocessed for probes;
+alternatively a small direct probe writer can use the same CSV positions.
+Several mesh blocks are needed to benefit from OpenMP task parallelism;
+a single block is effectively a one-thread run. No AMR is necessary.
+
+Estimated implementation is 400–600 lines of our problem generator plus
+runner/reader for a hydro crosscheck, reusing the boundary-map parser and
+physical units. A 24-grid pilot should be followed by 48×8×48 and, if useful,
+72×12×72 comparisons, each with finite CPU/wall limits and low output cadence.
+Based on the serial Brio-Wu reference throughput (~0.89 million zone-cycles
+per second with characteristic PPM), a 25-day solar-wind run might cost
+approximately 1–5 minutes at the coarse grid and 5–15 minutes at the medium
+grid, with <200 MB at coarse resolution. These are estimates: 3D HLLD cost,
+geometry and the actual local CFL bound require a pilot benchmark. A local
+MHD CFL bound may allow larger timesteps than the current solver's conservative
+global-cleaning-speed timestep, partly offsetting HLLD's cost.
+
+The principal scientific risk is magnetic boundary compatibility, rather than
+the mature interior solver. CT preserves discrete divergence only if initial
+face fields and boundary updates are compatible. The initial field should
+come from a discrete curl/vector potential. Overwriting the inner face Br at
+each timestep from independently changing daily maps can inject divergence
+even when the interior uses CT. Faraday's law requires a compatible tangential
+electric field. A frozen rotating Br map is compatible with the Parker
+electric field; independent daily Br changes require an additional inductive
+electric field, or an equivalent Btheta/velocity prescription not determined
+by Br alone. The user-boundary interface controls primitive/face ghost fields;
+no simple user EMF hook was found in the pinned code. A fully prescribed daily
+Br experiment may therefore need a small core hook and additional tests,
+bringing the total to roughly 700–1000 lines and appreciable validation work.
+
+A sensible sequence is (1) identical daily n/v/T, zero B, to isolate transport
+and geometry; (2) frozen rotating Br with consistent CT initialization and
+boundary electric field, applied identically in both models; and only then
+(3) the complete daily magnetic map after its inductive boundary condition is
+specified. Floors or HLLD fallbacks must be monitored; matching proton flux
+at one epoch would not itself validate the implementation. No model should
+be selected merely because it agrees better with spacecraft or CCMC data.
+
+Relevant pinned code:
+
+- [Point-mass source](https://github.com/PrincetonUniversity/athena/blob/e47fabb7dd5efb22e1e2c7ff193148d723e3e952/src/hydro/srcterms/pointmass.cpp)
+- [Spherical field-loop initialization and user boundaries](https://github.com/PrincetonUniversity/athena/blob/e47fabb7dd5efb22e1e2c7ff193148d723e3e952/src/pgen/field_loop_poles.cpp)
+- [Mesh callback interfaces](https://github.com/PrincetonUniversity/athena/blob/e47fabb7dd5efb22e1e2c7ff193148d723e3e952/src/mesh/mesh.hpp)
+- [Output formats](https://github.com/PrincetonUniversity/athena/blob/e47fabb7dd5efb22e1e2c7ff193148d723e3e952/src/outputs/outputs.cpp)
*** Add File: /mnt/c/Users/cabot/OneDrive/Documents/Research/Cambridge/X3I/mhd_llm/codex/solver/tests/athena_reference/README.md
+# Independent Brio-Wu comparison
+
+The frozen reference is an independently executed Athena++ 8192-cell
+HLLD/characteristic-PPM/SSPRK3 calculation, with gamma 2, discontinuity at
+x=0.5 and final time 0.1. It follows the classic Brio-Wu setup in the
+[official Athena tutorial](https://github.com/PrincetonUniversity/athena/wiki/1D-Shock-Tube)
+and the reference configuration discussed by
+[Stone et al. 2020](https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-4365/ab929b).
+
+`provenance.json` pins the official repository commit, archive checksum and
+configuration. The third-party source/build tree lives outside this project;
+only the frozen input, results, logs and our reproduction/analysis scripts
+are stored here. `python reproduce.py` downloads/verifies the pinned source
+if needed, builds with one job, and runs with one thread and finite resource
+limits. `python compare.py` regenerates `reference.csv`, `comparison.json`
+and the PNG/PDF figure from the raw tabular output.
+
+Against the independent reference, mean absolute density error decreases:
+
+| In-house test | n400 | n800 | n1600 | n6400 |
+|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
+| Baseline LLF/GLM | 0.02529 | 0.01899 | 0.01382 | 0.006954 |
+| Split GLM + local LLF | 0.02053 | 0.01477 | 0.01055 | — |
+
+The normal magnetic field remains exactly 0.75 in the saved in-house tests.
+Reference values are conservatively averaged onto each in-house grid before
+computing errors. The Brio-Wu CLI deliberately uses first spatial order to
+isolate the numerical flux; the production 3D solver uses MC reconstruction
+and SSPRK2 by default. This benchmark is consequently not a comprehensive
+test of every production reconstruction or geometry operation.
+
+Brio-Wu admits nonunique MHD wave patterns. The plateau values in Table 1 of
+[Dao and Nazarov's paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.09568), supplied by the
+separate literature extraction, correspond to a branch omitting an intermediate
+shock. The comparison JSON records samples against that table but does not
+treat it as a unique exact target for the full compound structure. The error
+table above uses the independent Athena numerical branch as the reference.
+
+The serial build and reference run consumed about 165 s wall time in total,
+with peak RSS about 174 MB; the actual simulation took about 95.5 CPU seconds.
+This verifies independent numerical convergence for a classic MHD problem.
+It does not establish convergence or observational accuracy of the solar-wind
+prediction, whose numerical-flux sensitivity remains material.
*** End Patch"));
